spot: Quarry cliff face (former quarry wall / main climbing crag)

detail.reason: The cache-able spot is the cliff BASE at parking level (no climbing). It is low ground beneath a wall, not a high overlook with a view down — fails the single dominant high-support signature.
At the base you face an 80-100 ft wall; the view is enclosed/blocked, not a broad open panorama.
Exact match: 'cut rock walls, ledges, talus and recesses at the base form natural niches (no digging)' — reach into a stone recess.
Niches/ledges/talus at or above ground, explicitly no digging required.
Stone is unambiguously the host feature — the dominant rock feature of the whole park.
Quarry/wetland standing water sits near the base and is not crossed, but it is not directly adjacent to the cliff face itself.
Forms the backdrop directly above the main parking lot; reachable in minutes, well under 3 mi, no water crossing to reach the base.
Base reached in minutes from parking on easy footing; note that reaching the wall ROUTES needs climbing/permit, but standing at base does not.
Opposite of concealed — it is the most prominent, dead-obvious feature towering directly over the parking lot, heavily visited by climbers.
A single continuous quarried wall, not a gap/saddle/notch between paired features.
Bare cut rock face; no prominent tree marker noted.
Cliff has discrete faces (the named Left/west face faces west); orientation of the main wall is not clearly east, so no clean cardinal match.
Setting is developed quarry core / open rock and parking, not a woods-meets-clearing forest edge.
Quarried wall is sheer, blocky and angular — not a rounded/domed/egg-shaped marker stone.
Blasted/cut quarry walls are sharp, stepped, blocky and faceted — a man-made angular rampart form.
Cliff seeps support Michaux's saxifrage and lichen/moss against the dark cut rock — plausible color contrast but not emphasized.
Host material is granite-gneiss (crystalline, quartz-bearing), but no notable sparkle/quartz seam called out here.
Granitic gneiss is light-grey; freshly cut quarry faces can read pale, though weathered walls are darker.
No reddish/iron-stained or golden warm-tone cue noted for the cut wall.
The quarry pit is a large basin/amphitheater, but the cliff-face spot itself is the wall, not a cup/bowl recess.
No confluence or watercourse bend at the cliff face.
No characteristic descent-then-rise approach to the base; it is right at parking grade.
Bolt anchors and named-route markings are small man-made marks on the wall, loosely matching a close-up confirming mark.
Faint echo only: the crag's named sub-area is the 'Left Face' reached by going around the left side — a 'left' nudge, but tied to a sibling spot.
Overhangs/roofs at the base are open to weather but offer shelter; partial match to a non-cave exposed niche.
No fixed marker-to-spot pace count associated with the cliff face.
